paragraphs: The day has two busy periods: preparation before opening and coordinated service during lunch and dinner rushes. Cutting must be fast and uniform, while salads, soup bases, and prepared ingredients must meet standards. During rushes, one worker can cover several stations, refilling, plating, and packing without pause. After closing, workers clean surfaces, organize refrigerators, and check expiration dates. Holidays can double the workload.
In one sentence: turn ingredients into a state cooks can use immediately. Washing, cutting, preparing, plating, and cleaning keep the kitchen moving from before opening through closing.
